text:
Matthew Schaefer won the Calder last season and has somehow found another gear. He's 19, playing 26:59 a night (up from 24:41), and has 21 points in 19 games after 59 in 82 as a rookie. He reached his 100th NHL game in Los Angeles and scored on the power play in it, and Markerzone ran a headline about him tying Bobby Orr in NHL history.

How much is real? Most of it. With him on the ice at five on five the Islanders take 52.8% of the expected goals, 6.4 points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at a 99th percentile rate last season. His last ten (13 points) we'd call partly real: the chances are up a little, but finishing is doing most of the work.

The skating is the thing to watch. His 84 bursts over 20 mph put him at the top of the NHL EDGE percentiles, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 36% of his shots coming off the rush (typical defenseman: 17%). Nineteen games is a small sample for the scoring. The ice time is not.
headline: Schaefer, 19, keeps adding minutes and history
